title.narrative: Building Resilience for Adaptation to Climate Change and Climate Variability in Agriculture in Saint Lucia

description.narrative:
The project will increase the resilience of an estimated 11 communities (82 sub-communities) across the four targeted agriculture regions in Saint Lucia through activities which are expected to improve farm productivity, water and livelihood security; and reduce vulnerability to natural hazards, climate variability (CV), and climate change (CC). An estimated 12,000 farmers and their families are expected to be direct beneficiaries ofthe Project. The Project outcomes are: (a) Increased farm productivity with improved livelihood security, incomes and new farm areas brought under production in the Project areas.
(b) Increased productivity and competitiveness in resilient small farming systems with improved livelihood security, increased incomes, employment generation and household food security.
(c) Established information and communication systems to support adaptive capacities for the resilience of small farming systems, improved livelihood security, income generation, CC and DRR.
(a) Component 1: Building resilience and sustainability of farming systems through interventions for water security, soil conservation and management. This component will see the reduction in landslips, and soil erosion on farms through creation of updated maps, vulnerability analysis, and field practices. It will also increase access to on-farm water through infrastructure for rainwater harvesting and the provision of drip irrigation infrastructure. The project will also build soil resilience using compost and other organic material and the construction of six outdoor facilities for production and practical demonstration of soil building materials. (b) Component 2: Establishing green agro-parks, including the use of solar energy, for increased efficiency in resilient farming systems. This component is expected to increase competitiveness along the production value chain using renewable energy and to incorporate the use of a green approach through the establishment of two green agroparks
